title: TOP 15 Unreal Places on Earth Even Scientists Can't Explain
fullText: There is a lake in Antarctica that has been sealed off from the outside world for 15 million years. It sits under 4 km of solid ice. No sunlight has touched it since before humans evolved. When Russian scientists finally drilled through the ice in 2012 and reached the water below, they found life. Bacteria, genetic sequences that match nothing in any database. [music] organisms that had been evolving in total darkness, in total isolation for longer than the human species has existed. In the Amazon rainforest, there is a river that boils. The water reaches 86° C. Fish that fall in are cooked instantly. Locals have known about it for centuries. Scientists ignored the reports as legend for nearly a 100red years because there is [music] no volcano within 700 km and the standard geological model says a boiling river should not exist there. The river exists. The temperature is real. And [music] in 2011, a geoysicist finally verified what indigenous shamans had been saying the entire time. In the mountains of Norway, strange [music] lights have been appearing in the sky over a valley called Hestalin for at least 200 years. Sometimes red, [music] sometimes white, sometimes blue. They hover, they dart, some last for hours. Since 1984, an automated scientific station has been recording them. [music] Roughly 20 sightings per week. And after four decades of monitoring by physicists from three universities, the leading explanation is still [music] quote, "We do not know." And on a small island off the coast of Yemen, there is a tree that bleeds. Its sap runs red. The trees grow nowhere else on Earth. Roughly a third [music] of all the plant species on the island exist only there, nowhere else on the planet. When British naturalists [music] first documented it, they called the island the strangest place on Earth. That was in 1834. [music] It has not gotten less strange since. This is our countdown of the [music] 15 most bizarre places on Earth that even scientists cannot explain. Stay until the end because number one is that Antarctic lake and what came up from underneath the ice has been changing what biology thinks it knows about life for over a decade. Before we start, drop a comment telling us where you are watching from right now. We want to see how many countries this video reaches. Number 15, Devil's Kettle Falls. Judge CR Magny State [music] Park, Minnesota. On the Brule River in northeastern Minnesota, close to the Canadian border, a waterfall splits in two. The eastern half [music] drops roughly 15 m and continues downstream exactly as a waterfall should. The western half falls into a hole in the rock and nobody knows where the water goes. For over a century, park rangers and researchers have tried to trace it. Fluorescent dye has been poured in. Pingpong balls by the hundreds. GPS trackers. Colored logs. In every documented attempt, the tracers have simply not reappeared. Not downstream. Not in Lake Superior, not anywhere. [music] In 2017, hydraologists from the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources conducted a study using precise flow measurements upstream and downstream of the falls. Their results indicated that the total water volume was consistent above and below the split, meaning the water is rejoining the river somewhere below the visible falls. But that explanation raises a bigger question. If the water is rejoining, why do the tracers never appear? Ping pong balls float. Dye stains rock. If the water flows through a simple underground channel and reemerges downstream, something, anything, should have come out by now. Nothing has. The devil's kettle continues to swallow half of the Brule River. The tracers never reappear. And the official explanation offered by every geologist who has studied the site boils down to a single phrase. We think we understand it. We cannot prove we do. Number 14, Chaet Tempishka, [music] the boiling river, Amazon Basin, Peru. For nearly a century, geologists dismissed [music] it as folklore. The Ashona people of the central Peruvian Amazon spoke about a [music] river deep in the jungle where the water boiled. Steam rose from the surface. Fish that fell in were cooked. Shamans considered it sacred. Anyone [music] who touched it died. Scientists said it could not exist. Boiling rivers require a heat source. volcanoes, geothermal vents. The nearest active volcano was over 700 kilometers away. The Amazon basin lacks the geological features that produce hot springs elsewhere in the world. In 2011, a Peruvian American geoysicist named Andre Russo, then a doctoral student at Southern Methodist University, followed his grandfather's stories into the jungle. He found the river. He measured the temperature. 86° [music] C just below boiling along a stretch approximately 6.4 km long in a river up to 25 m wide and 6 m deep. Russo's subsequent research published in his book The Boiling River and in the peer-reviewed journal Nature confirmed what indigenous communities [music] had been reporting for centuries. The river is real. The temperature is real and the heat source is not volcanic. The current explanation, still incomplete, is that the river is fed by hot geothermal water flowing up through fault lines in the Earth's crust from deep aquifers heated by residual geothermal energy. The specific configuration that produces such extreme temperatures without a volcanic source remains, in Russo's own words, one of the most puzzling geothermal anomalies on the planet. [music] The Asheninka call the river Shanai Tempishka, boiled with the heat of the sun. They knew it was there for hundreds of [music] years. Science needed a jungle expedition and a temperature gauge to catch [music] up. Number 13, the fairy circles. Namibbrand Nature Reserve, Namibia. Stretch a piece of grassland across the Namib Desert for hundreds of kilome. Then imagine that grassland is dotted in a pattern so regular it looks designed with circles of bare earth. Perfect circles ranging from 2 to 15 meters in diameter. [music] Empty. No grass grows inside. And around each circle, the grass is unusually tall and dense. Now scale that across an area larger than Ireland. Aerial surveys by the University of Hamburg and the University [music] of Namibia have documented millions of ferry circles across a narrow band of desert running from Angola through Namibia into South Africa. Their spatial distribution is highly regular. Statistical analysis published in the proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences has shown that the circles are spaced with a mathematical precision typically seen in engineered systems. Two competing theories have been fighting for dominance for over 40 years. Neither has won. The first hypothesis championed by ecologist Norbert Jurgens of the University of Hamburg argues that the circles are created by sand termites. Colonies of samotermy's aloaris feed on the roots of grass in circular patterns creating bare zones that trap moisture benefiting the termites during [music] the dry season. Jurgens's team documented termite activity at nearly every circle they excavated. The second hypothesis championed by physicist Stefan gets of the University [music] of Gingan argues that the circles emerge from plant self-organization. Grassroots compete for scarce water and mathematical modeling shows that the observed patterns match what would emerge from vegetation reacting to water stress alone. No termites required. Geten's models have been published multiple times, most recently in the journal Perspectives in Plant Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics. Both sides site field evidence. Neither has been able to definitively [music] disprove the other. As of 2024, both hypotheses remain scientifically viable. The Hima people of Namibia offer a third explanation. According to their oral tradition documented by ethnographer David of Brigham Y Young University, the circles are the footprints of the gods. Their ancestors have been walking that desert for thousands of years. And they say the circles have always been there and always will be. Termites, mathematics, or gods, take your pick. All three explanations are still on the table. Number 12, the Nazca lines. Nazca desert, Peru. For 2,000 years, they were invisible from the ground. The Nazca lines, enormous figures etched into the desert floor of southern Peru, depicting monkeys, spiders, hummingbirds, whales, and geometric shapes stretching for hundreds of meters, can only be fully seen from the air. The people who made them, the Nazca culture, existed between roughly 500 B.CE and 500 CE. They had no aircraft. 20th century archaeologists documented over 700 figures. The debate over their purpose has continued for a 100red years. Then artificial intelligence [music] changed everything. In 2019, a team led by archaeologist Masado Sakai of Yamagata University in Japan, working with researchers from IBM, began systematically analyzing satellite and aerial imagery of the Nazca region using machine learning algorithms. Their initial [music] published results identified 143 previously unknown Nazca figures, doubling the known count. In 2023, an updated study in the journal PNAS Nexus reported [music] that the same AI assisted analysis had identified over 300 additional figures. Field verification confirmed many of them. Some were smaller than earlier discoveries. Some depicted animals that had not appeared in previous inventories, and some were located in regions that had never been surveyed on foot. The total known Nazca figure count has now more than doubled in less than a decade. Sakai's team believes that thousands more may exist across the region still undetected. The bigger question, what were they [music] for remains open? Multiple theories have been proposed since Peruvian archaeologist Toribio Mahia Cespe first described the lines in the 1920s. Astronomical calendars, ritual pathways, water divination, offerings to deities, communication with beings above. None has achieved scholarly consensus. The lines are real. The scale is verified. The purpose is [music] not. And every year, artificial intelligence finds more of them buried under centuries of desert dust, still waiting for someone to explain what they were meant to say. Number 11. Mobile cave, Constansa County, Romania. In 1986, [music] workers surveying land for a power plant in southern Romania drilled into a limestone [music] hillside and hit a cavity. When the first cavers descended into it, they knew immediately that they had found something extraordinary. The air burned their eyes. Oxygen levels were roughly [music] 1/3 of normal atmospheric concentration. Carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide levels were by any surface standard toxic, and the [music] cave was full of animals. Mobile cave had been sealed off from the outside world for approximately 5.5 million years. Studies published by cave biologist Serban Sarbu of Emil [music] Rakovitza Institute of Speliology have documented 48 species living inside mobile. Of those 33 exist only there. Water scorpions, [music] cave adapted leeches, blind spiders, a species of caved dwelling centipede found nowhere else on Earth. The ecosystem does not depend on sunlight. Instead, it is fueled by chemosynthesis, bacteria that metabolize hydrogen sulfide and methane, converting inorganic chemistry into energy. Everything in Mobile eats the bacteria or eats something that eats the bacteria. The food chain is autonomous. Mobile is one of only two known cave ecosystems on Earth that operate independently of surface sunlight. The other, discovered in 1996 in Israel, contains fewer endemic species. Access is restricted. Sarbu's institute limits entry to a small [music] number of qualified researchers per year and full protective gear is mandatory. According to Saru, breathing the unfiltered air for more than a few minutes causes headaches, dizziness, and if extended, permanent lung damage. The organisms inside have been evolving on their own for over 5 million years. What they will become given another 5 million is a question no biology textbook can answer. The cave is being watched very carefully from a distance. Number 10, Lake Natron, Arouchia region, Tanzania. In the northern Tanzanian rift valley, there is a lake that turns animals into stone. Not metaphorically, physically, chemically, biologically. The bodies of birds, bats, and insects that land on Lake Natron and die are preserved in a rigid calcified state [music] that looks like they have been dipped in liquid stone. Lake Natron's water has a pH between 9 and 10.5. Alkaline enough to burn skin. Combined with dissolved sodium carbonate and other minerals leeched from the surrounding volcanic geology, the water functions like a natural imbalming solution. When an animal dies in or near the lake, the chemistry begins immediately. Soft tissue [music] dehydrates. Minerals infiltrate the tissue. The corpse hardens. Preservation happens fast. Photographer Nick Brandt documented the phenomenon in his 2013 [music] book, Across the Ravaged Land. His photographs taken along the shoreline of Lake Natron show flamingos, doves, bats, and swallows petrified in lielike poses, wings extended, eyes still visible, feet still gripping perches. Ecological studies published [music] by the Tanzania Wildlife Research Institute have confirmed that despite its extreme [music] chemistry, Lake Natron is not lifeless. Lesser flamingos have adapted to breed on the salt flats that appear seasonally in the lakes's shallows. The extreme alkalinity discourages predators. Millions of flamingos raise their young in one of the most hostile chemical environments on the planet. Around them, the calcified remains of birds that were less fortunate stand upright on the shore. [music] Number nine, Sootra Island, Yemen. It has been called the strangest place on Earth. Its landscape has been compared to alien planets and roughly a third of the plant species growing on Sootra Island exist [music] nowhere else in the world. Sootra sits in the Indian Ocean roughly 240 km off the coast of Yemen. Geologists estimate that it has been separated from the African mainland for approximately [music] 20 million years. That isolation has allowed the plants and animals on the island to evolve along paths that diverged from the [music] rest of the world in the middle of the meioene. The most famous species is Draina Cineabari, the dragon's blood tree. Its trunk splits into dozens of branches that form a dense umbrella-shaped canopy at the top. When cut, the tree bleeds a deep red resin. Ancient Greek and Roman traders considered the resin, called dragon's blood, magical. It has been used in medicine, magic, and dye for over 2,000 years. Botanical surveys by the Royal Botanic Gardens Q and the Environment Protection Authority of Yemen have documented over 800 plant species on Sootra. [music] Roughly 275 are endemic found on Soototra and nowhere else. The cucumber tree [music] Dendroicio Sootrana is the only tree species in the entire cucumber family. It has a bulbous water storing [music] trunk that looks like a green bottle sitting in the ground with branches growing from the top. Bottle trees adenium obesum sootranum have swollen gray trunks and blossom with pink flowers that seem to glow against the barren rock. Zoological surveys have identified 90 endemic bird species, [music] 700 endemic insect species and multiple lizard and snake species that exist only on the island. Almost half of Sotra's reptile species are found nowhere else. UNESCO inscribed Sotra as a world heritage site in 2008, describing it as one of the most biodiversity rich and distinct islands in the world. Ongoing conflict in Yemen has limited scientific access since 2015. What remains to be discovered on Sootra after 20 million years of parallel evolution is a question no one is currently in a position to answer. Number eight, Eternal [music] Flame Falls, Chestnut Ridge Park, New York, USA. In a small park outside Buffalo, New York, there is a [music] waterfall. Behind the waterfall, there is a small al cove in the shale rock. And [music] inside the alcove, there is a flame. The flame flickers behind the falling water. It burns roughly 20 cm high. It has been observed continuously by park visitors and rangers for over a century. It is fueled by natural gas seeping from the rock behind the al cove and it should not be there. Natural gas seeps like this are common in the shale richch Appalachian region. What is unusual about eternal flame falls is the source and the temperature of the shale that produces the gas. Standard geological theory of natural gas formation requires temperatures of at least 100° Celsius in the source rock. According to a 2013 study published in the journal Marine and Petroleum Geology by geologist Joseeppe Etiopi of Italy's National Institute of Geoysics and Volcanology and AR Shimlman of Indiana University, the shale beneath eternal flame falls is only around 45 to 55° C. Not hot enough by half. Eddie Opie and Shimlman's study concluded that the gas being emitted at Eternal Flame Falls cannot be explained by conventional [music] thermogenic or biogenic gas formation models. The origin, in their published words, remains an open geological question. The flame burns behind the waterfall. Hikers have been standing behind it for photographs since [music] the 1920s. Occasionally, the wind extinguishes it and the next visitor rekindles it with a lighter. Nobody knows exactly where the gas [music] is coming from or how it got there. Number seven, Dean's Blue Hole, Long Island, Bahamas. From above, it looks like a hole in the sea, a circular patch of ink dark water surrounded by turquoise shallows and pale sand. Divers who swim over the edge feel the difference in temperature before they see the drop. The drop [music] is 202 m straight down. Dean's Blue Hole on Long Island in the Bahamas is the second deepest known underwater sinkhole in the world. It was the deepest until 2016 when the Dragon Hole in the South China Sea was measured at 300 m. Both are what oceanographers call blue holes, vertical caves formed during past ice ages when sea levels were lower. Underwater surveys by researcher Kenny Broad of the University of Miami, working with the National Geographic [music] Society, have documented Dean's Blue Hole as vertical for the top 100 m, then widening into a cavern approximately 25 m wide at the base. The water in the deepest sections contains almost no oxygen. Below roughly 20 meters, hydrogen sulfide from decomposing organic matter forms a chemocline, a boundary layer where anorobic conditions begin. Life exists below the chemocline. Bacteria that metabolize sulfur. Microorganisms that survive in conditions comparable to those on early Earth or on other planets. NASA's astrobiology program has studied blue holes as analoges for potential extraterrestrial environments. The bottom of Dean's blue hole is silt. Below the silt, there is more cave. According to Broad's research, side passages branch [music] from the main chamber and extend into the surrounding limestone in directions and to distances that have not been fully mapped. The free diving world record for depth was set at Dean's Blue Hole in 2016 by New Zealander William TrouBridge, who descended to 124 m on a [music] single breath. The bottom at 202 m is beyond human reach without technical scuba equipment. What lies in the side passages is beyond human reach entirely so far. If you are still watching, hit subscribe. Rocks are not supposed to be that many colors. In the Gansu province of northwestern China, sandstone mountains rise from the desert in stripes of red, orange, yellow, green, and blue. The colors run in horizontal bands across cliffs and ridges that [music] stretch for hundreds of kilome. In late afternoon light, the mountains appear painted as if a giant had brushed watercolors across the landscape. They are not painted, they are stone. The Jang Dangia land form is composed of layered sandstone and other [music] sedimentary rocks deposited over approximately 24 million years during the Cretaceous period. Different mineral compositions in each layer produce different colors. Iron oxide deposits produce reds and oranges. Sulfur and iron sulfides [music] produce yellows. Chlorite and other iron magnesium silicates produce greens. Geological analysis by the China University of Geossciences has [music] confirmed that the striping is a result of gradual accumulation. Each colored layer represents a different depositional environment over millions of years. Compression, uplift, and erosion by wind and water carve the mountains into their current [music] shape. The mystery is not why the colors exist. It is how they line up so precisely across such a vast area. Perfect horizontal bands extending across [music] ridges separated by kilometers matching layer for layer without geological interruption. The Jangy Dangia was inscribed as part of the China Dangia World Heritage Site by UNESCO in [music] 2010. Photography does not do it justice. Neither does description. The colors are real. The scale is real. [music] And no other place on Earth looks like this. Number five, the Lake Michigan Triangle. Michigan, USA. Between the western shore of Michigan and the eastern shore of Wisconsin, there is a stretch of Lake Michigan where things go missing. Ships, aircraft, people, over [music] 40 documented disappearances in the last 200 years, many with no explanation. The most famous case is the griffin. In 1679, French explorer Renee Rober Cavalier Sure De Lasal launched a wooden ship called La Griffin on Lake Michigan. On its return voyage from Green Bay to Niagara, loaded with furs and crewed by six men, the ship sailed into a storm on September 18th, 1679, and was never seen again. No wreckage has ever been positively identified. In 1937, a lumber freighter called OM McFarland vanished from Lake [music] Michigan while its captain was on route to check the cargo. The rest of the crew reported that Captain George Donner locked himself in his cabin for the night. When he was called for breakfast, he did not answer. The cabin was empty. Locked from the inside. Airplane disappearances have been the most puzzling. On June 23rd, 1950, Northwest Airlines flight 25501, a Douglas DC4 [music] with 58 people aboard, vanished over Lake Michigan during a night flight from New York to Minneapolis. It was at the time the deadliest commercial aviation accident in US history. Despite decades of underwater searches, no significant wreckage has ever been located. Marine researcher Valerie Van Heast has documented over 300 shipwrecks in Lake Michigan since the 1600s. Roughly a third of them are missing without confirmed location. Skeptics attribute the disappearances to storms, freshwater squalls, and the lakes's depth, which reaches 281 m in the central basin. Believers point to the concentration of vanishings in a specific area and to accounts by mariners over centuries [music] who describe magnetic anomalies, sudden fogs, and inexplicable equipment failures. The lake keeps what it takes, and it has taken a lot. Number four, Lazona del Silencio, [music] Mapimei Biosphere Reserve, Mexico. In the northern Mexican desert, roughly 40 km south of the town of Sibios, there is a region called the zone of silence. Radios do not work there. Television signals do not penetrate. Compasses spin. Watches slow. And in July 1970, an American Athena rocket carrying two containers of radioactive [music] cobalt 57 was fired from White Sands, New Mexico, and crashed there on the first try, as if the desert had pulled it in. The US Air Force spent weeks [music] recovering the rocket and the radioactive payload. During the operation, technicians reported extensive equipment malfunctions. Radios failed. Compasses gave inconsistent readings. Communication with the outside world was intermittent. [music] The Mexican government subsequently established the Mapi Biosphere Reserve to protect the area's unique ecosystem, which includes species found nowhere else in Mexico. But local witnesses whose accounts have been documented by Mexican journalists and by researchers including geologist Harry de Laena of the autonomous University of Chihuahua [music] have described strange phenomena for generations. Lights in the sky, unusual behavior in electronic equipment. Meteorites. [music] Over 600 documented meteorite fragments recovered from an area roughly 50 square kilm. Scientific explanations for the electromagnetic [music] anomalies center on the region's geology. High concentrations of magnetite in the local iron ore deposits can distort magnetic fields and interfere with radio signals. The high meteorite density has been attributed to the area's position. Though the specific pattern of impact frequency has not been fully explained, nothing about the zone of silence violates known physics. But every visitor's compass agrees on the same thing. Number three, the hum. It is not a place. It is a sound. And it is heard right now by an estimated four to 5% of the world's population. The hum is a low frequency persistent noise that people in dozens of locations [music] around the world report hearing, often at night, often in a quiet setting, often from a source [music] they cannot locate. Some describe it as a distant diesel engine idling, others as a low frequency [music] vibration felt as much as heard. It has been reported in Ta New Mexico, in Bristol, England, in Windsor, Ontario, in Auckland, New Zealand, and in dozens of other locations across five continents. Research published in the Journal of Scientific Exploration and by the World Hum Map and Database Project has documented consistent characteristics. The frequency range is typically between 30 and 80 hertz. It is inaudible to some people standing next to those who hear it clearly. It persists for hours. Attempts to record it with standard microphones often fail, which has fueled the debate over whether it is external sound or internal perception. Multiple theories exist. Industrial equipment, distant infrastructure, [music] geological activity, tonitis at a specific frequency, sound from ocean waves converting to seismic vibrations. None of them explain all cases. The most extensively studied case is the ta hum in New Mexico. Investigations by the University of New Mexico and Sandia National Laboratories in the 1990s failed to identify a source. The TA hum still persists. Residents still hear it. Every year, new sufferers report the same experience. A sound that no equipment can definitively record. Heard by roughly one in 20 people in the community, driving some to insomnia and psychological distress. The hum is real to those who hear it. It is not real to those who cannot and in that gap science has not been able to build a bridge that everyone can walk across. Number two, [music] the Hestilin lights. Trundellog County, Norway. In a valley in central Norway called Hestelin, [music] roughly 30 km long and thinly populated, strange lights have been appearing in the sky for at least 200 years. Sometimes they are white, sometimes yellow, sometimes red or blue. They range in size from small orbs to [music] objects several meters across. They hover. They move slowly. They dart at speeds that ordinary aircraft cannot match. Some last for seconds, others last for more than [music] an hour. From the late 1970s to 1984, sightings became so frequent that residents were reporting them almost every night. In 1984, physicist Erling Strand established Project Hestin, a scientific research initiative [music] dedicated to documenting the phenomenon systematically. Since 1998, an automated observation station has monitored the valley continuously. Cameras, radar, magnetometers, and spectral analyzers record every anomalous event. Data has been published in peer-reviewed journals and shared with researchers from Ostold University College in Norway and the University of Padua [music] in Italy. Roughly 20 anomalous sightings are recorded per week. Analysis of the light spectrum has revealed the presence of elements including silicon, iron, aluminum, and scandium. In some cases, the light emissions have been consistent with plasma ionized gas. Though the mechanism producing plasma balls of that size and duration in open atmosphere remains unexplained. Erling Strand and physicist Masimo Durani of the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics have proposed multiple hypotheses. Ionization of dust in the air. PZO electric effects from custal stress in the local geology. Combustion of naturally occurring gases. None of them explain all the observed characteristics. The Hestline lights are not folklore. They have been recorded by scientific instruments for over [music] four decades. The data is public. The lights continue to appear. And after 200 years of observation, 40 years of scientific study, and thousands of documented sightings, the leading explanation from the physicists [music] who have spent their careers studying them remains a variation on the same sentence. We do not know what they are. Number one, Lake Vastto, Antarctica. 4 kilometers beneath the East Antarctic ice sheet, sealed off from the outside world for approximately 15 million years, there is a lake, not a small one. Lake Vastto is roughly 250 km long and 50 km wide, comparable in surface area to Lake Ontario. It contains an estimated 5,400 cm of water. It is the largest and deepest of Antarctica's more than 400 known subglacial lakes. And until 2012, no human hand had ever touched its water. The lake was first discovered indirectly. In the 1960s and 1970s, Russian [music] and British scientists analyzing airborne radar surveys of the Antarctic ice sheet noticed an unusual smoothness in one region of the ice above the Russian Vastto research station. The smoothness indicated that the ice was floating over a large body of liquid water beneath. Further surveys through the 1990s using seismic radar and satellite alimemetry data mapped the lakes's dimensions. Ice cores drilled by an international team from the Russian Antarctic expedition revealed that the ice above Lake Vastto was over 400,000 years old at the base. Meaning the lake had been sealed off from the atmosphere for longer than modern humans have existed. Estimates of how long Lake Vostto has been isolated from the surface range widely, but the geological evidence suggests the lake may have been separated from the outside world for 15 to 25 million years. In February 2012, after decades of drilling from Vastto Station, a Russian team led by Valeri Lucan of the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute finally reached the surface of the lake at a depth of 3,769 m. Water rose up the bore hole. Samples were collected. Analysis began. The samples contained bacteria. DNA sequencing published in a controversial 2013 paper in plus one by microbiologist Scott Rogers of Bowling Green State University identified thousands of unique genetic [music] sequences. Some matched known organisms. Some matched partial sequences from bacteria found in hydrothermal environments, in deep ocean vents, and in extreme salt lakes. And roughly onethird of the sequences did not match anything in any existing genetic database. The findings were criticized. Contamination concerns from the drilling process were raised. [music] Rogers team defended their methodology. Follow-up studies have continued to identify anomalous genetic material in Lake Vastto samples, though the debate over contamination versus native organisms is ongoing. What is not in dispute is that Lake Vastto [music] is one of the most extreme environments on Earth. Water pressure at the surface of the lake is roughly 350 atmospheres. Temperatures are near freezing. Oxygen concentrations based on models of ice lake gas exchange may be up to 50 times higher than in typical freshwater lakes. Complete darkness, complete isolation for at least 15 million years. If life exists in Lake Vastto and the evidence suggests something does, it has been evolving on its own path for longer than the primate order has existed. Whatever organisms are down there have not seen sunlight since before humans, chimpanzees, gorillas or bonobos [music] existed as separate species. Russian drilling operations at Vastto Station have continued in the years since 2012. The strategy [music] has been to sample water that rises up the borehole rather than to physically enter the lake, minimizing contamination risk. Debates over whether more invasive exploration should be permitted are ongoing among the international scientific community. There are other subglacial Antarctic lakes as well. Lake Willins sampled by a US team in 2013. Lake Mercer sampled in 2019. Both contained microbial life. Both are smaller than Vastto and less isolated. Lake Vastto is the largest, the deepest, the oldest, the most sealed, and the least sampled. What lives in the majority of its 5,400 cub km of water? What has been evolving without sunlight, without atmosphere, without competition for the entire history of the human genus is unknown. The ice above [music] it is 4 km thick. The lake beneath is dark, cold, and old. And the next drilling season is planned. What comes up the bore hole next is a question every biologist on Earth is watching for. Because if life has been running its own experiment down there for 15 million years, nobody has any idea what it has become. 15 [music] places. A boiling river in the Amazon that indigenous shamans knew about for centuries before science admitted it existed. fairy circles in Namibia that termites, mathematics, or gods might have made. A lake in Tanzania that turns [music] birds to stone. An island off Yemen where a third of the plants exist nowhere else on Earth. A flame burning behind a waterfall in New York fed by gas that geology cannot fully explain. A blue hole in the Bahamas 202 meters deep with side passages that keep going. Painted mountains in China that stretch for hundreds of kilome. A great lake in America that swallows ships and planes [music] without leaving debris. A Mexican desert that jams radios and pulls in meteorites. A sound heard by one in 20 people that no microphone can definitively capture. lights that have been dancing over a Norwegian valley for 200 years and are still dancing tonight. And a lake under 4 kilometers of Antarctic ice sealed from the [music] world for 15 million years holding water and organisms that nobody has yet seen. Every one of these places has been studied, some for decades, some for centuries. And every one of them at some point in the investigation has forced a scientist to say the same three words that science is not supposed to be comfortable with. We do not know.
